label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8)
explanation: Fires essentially only on the delimiter step (99.95% of activations at t == L, plus a handful at recall_idx 1). It never fires during the original or copy phases. Firing depends strongly on sequence length: at the delimiter it fires about 42% of the time for L=9 and 26% for L=8, falls off fast for L=7 and below, and is almost never active for L<=5. L=9 alone carries 60% of the activation mass and L=8 30%. Among long sequences, whether it fires depends on content in a spread-out way. It is more likely when the first token is n, f, h, 0, i or u, or when k or p appear in the middle of the sequence, and less likely when the first token is w, a, r, v, t or y. No single token condition captures this (adding such conditions raises F1 only from 0.49 to about 0.52). Magnitude follows the same pattern: the top examples are L=9 sequences starting with n or f that contain k or p.
